questions.q: How does the SGD update $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta \cdot \frac{1}{B}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_t} \nabla \ell_i(w_t)$ differ from full-batch GD?
options: It averages gradients over a random mini-batch of $B$ examples instead of all $N$
It uses a larger learning rate than full-batch GD
It computes the exact gradient but skips some steps
It sums instead of averaging the gradients
questions.explain: Full batch averages all $N$ per-example gradients; SGD averages only a random subset $\mathcal{B}_t$ of size $B$, making each step much cheaper.

questions.q: On average, how does the mini-batch gradient compare to the full-batch gradient?
options: It is always exactly equal to the full gradient
It is systematically biased toward the global minimum
It always points in a random direction unrelated to the full gradient
It points the same way on average (unbiased), but each individual estimate is noisy
questions.explain: A random subset's average gradient is an unbiased estimate of the full average, but different batches give different estimates, which is why the SGD path looks jumpy.

questions.q: With the lab's dataset of 64 examples and batch size $B = 8$, how many SGD steps cost the same compute as one full-batch step (⚖️ Equal compute)?
questions.explain: One full-batch step processes all 64 examples; each SGD step processes 8, so $64/8 = 8$ SGD steps match it. ($512 = 64 \times 8$ multiplies instead of divides.)

questions.q: In the lab, full batch gets stuck in the dip near (−3.5, −4.2). What happens to SGD as you change the batch size?
options: Large batches escape more often because their gradient is more accurate
Small batches (1–2) almost always escape; large batches (8+) usually stay stuck too
Batch size has no effect on escaping
SGD always escapes, regardless of batch size
questions.explain: Smaller batches mean noisier gradients, a 'shake' that can push the ball out of a shallow dip. Large batches behave almost like full batch. Noise is not a guarantee, and too much keeps the optimizer jittering near the bottom.
